subject.title: Pause blocked background Claude CLI auth probes

question: Should any five-second Claude auth-status timeout suppress background Auto CLI probing for six hours, or should the long cooldown require repeated or more specific evidence of a blocked Keychain subprocess?
rationale: The probe outcome only reports a timeout and cannot distinguish the reported Keychain modal from ordinary CLI or system slowness, so the acceptable compatibility tradeoff requires repository-owner intent.

options.title: Escalate after repeated timeouts
options.body: Use a short initial backoff and extend it only after repeated timeouts, limiting disruption from transient slowness while still stopping recurring prompts.

options.title: Keep six hours for every timeout
options.body: Accept that any timeout may suppress background Auto CLI use for six hours in exchange for the strongest prompt-loop protection.

options.title: Coalesce without persistent cooldown
options.body: Share concurrent probes but retain per-refresh timeout behavior, avoiding upgrade-visible provider suppression while leaving periodic prompt recurrence possible.

recommendation.title: Escalate after repeated timeouts
recommendation.body: Use a short initial backoff and extend it only after repeated timeouts, limiting disruption from transient slowness while still stopping recurring prompts.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice changes established Claude provider routing and persisted upgrade behavior, and steipete merged the current preflight implementation.
